newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner sees 97 as record setting year.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner sees 97 as record setting year.

text.p: Bolstered by its October merger with Turner Broadcasting System plus three consecutive $100 million movie hits over the summer season, Time Warner Inc said Tuesday it is "strategically complete" and expects a "very strong" and record-setting year in 1997.

The company said the performance of the Turner Networks remains outstanding. TNT, CNN and TBS Superstation is each now in over 70 million homes and the Cartoon Network in 40 million, the company said.
And TNT became the No. 1 rated basic cable network in primetime, Time Warner said.
"At this point I expect 1997 to be another very strong year, even a record-setting year," Time Warner Chief Executive Gerald Levin said in a statement released with the company's earnings.
He said he is very pleased with the quality and pace of its integration efforts with Turner.
TBS has acquired exclusive network TV rights to several Warner Bros. films and the Cartoon Network is benefiting from Warner Bros.' programming, Levin said.

Fourth quarter EBITDA for Time Inc, the company's publishing division, was $200 million, up 14 percent, compared to $175 million a year earlier, the company said. For 1996, EBITDA from continuing operations reached $535 million, up 12 percent, as compared to $476 million in 1995, the company said.

The company said its Warner Music Group posted fourth-quarter EBITDA of $290 million, compared to $295 million in 1995. For the full year, the company said EBITDA was $744 million, compared to $690 million for 1995, which includes an $85 million one-time charge.

Fourth-quarter EBITDA for the Cable Networks division was $162 million, up 22 percent, versus a pro forma $133 million a year earlier. For 1996, pro forma EBITDA was a record $547 million, a 9 percent increase over the pro forma $502 million that would have been recorded for 1995, the company said.

Fourth quarter EBITDA from Warner Bros was $123 million, versus $121 million a year earlier, the company said. For 1996, EBITDA was a record $546 million, an 11 percent increase over the $490 million earned in 1995, Time Warner said.

In the fourth quarter, Time Warner Cable posted a combined EBITDA of $526 million, up 15 percent from the comparable prior-year period pro forma results that reflect all of the cable mergers, acquisitions and partnerships from the beginning of 1995, the company said.
The company said Time Warner Cable now serves about 12.3 million subscribers and its 19 million homes passed is nearly 20 percent of total U.S. television households.
"The business units of Time Warner continue to lead their industries," Levin said.

Time Warner said all its international advertiser-supported networks are being consolidated under the Cable Networks Group and Time Warner said it is "looking at a number of alternatives" for New Line Cinema and Castle Rock Entertainment.
The studio's summer lineup of three consecutive $100 million plus hits Twister, Eraser and A Time To Kill was a first in movie history, Levin added.
And in television, he said, Warner Bros continues to lead the TV ratings with ER and Friends, as well as one of the season's new hits, Suddenly Susan."
